findings.evidence: Before delegating any step, ask: what does a subagent give here that the main thread lacks: isolation from a large search, a specialized registered agent, or parallel work? If none, run it directly. When it does help, name an agent type that exists (built-ins: `Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`...)
findings.fix: Cut this to the command-specific fact: 'A context: fork body runs as one subagent task and cannot wait for approval; keep approval gates in the main thread.' Drop the general when-to-delegate advice and the list of built-in agents, because the harness already provides subagent dispatch.

findings.evidence: A same-named skill in `.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/` shadows the command with no warning ... Check before writing (Workflow step 2).
findings.fix: Delete this Gotcha bullet. Workflow step 2 (line 15) already states the shadowing fact and the check, so here it only repeats tokens.

findings.evidence: Step 2 inlines an 11-line collision reply template (lines 17-25) in the middle of the phased workflow
findings.fix: Move the collision reply template to a 'Name collision' section in references/patterns.md. Leave a one-line trigger in step 2: 'If any exists, write nothing and read the Name collision section of references/patterns.md.' This keeps the Process pattern's steps scannable.

findings.evidence: {"query":"Create a prompt template for asking an AI to review pull requests.","should_trigger":false}
findings.fix: Relabel this query or replace it. The description triggers on a user who 'keeps pasting the same long prompt' and wants 'one thing to type', so a reusable PR-review prompt is a plausible positive. Replace it with an unambiguous near-miss, for example 'Write a CLAUDE.md section telling Claude how to review PRs in this repo'.

findings.evidence: look for `<name>` in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` and the target commands directory
findings.fix: Also check the other commands scope before writing: `~/.claude/commands/<name>.md` when writing a project command, and `.claude/commands/<name>.md` when writing a personal one. State which one the user gets on a clash and handle it with the same template. As written, a project /release that clashes with an existing personal /release is never flagged.

findings.evidence: The release eval expects a command that "keeps the transcript's order (main and up to date, clean tree, npm test, npm version, push with tags, npm publish)". However, the fixture starts with `git checkout main` and `git pull --ff-only` before checking cleanliness. Workflow step 1 requires proposing a safer order and obtaining approval when a side effect precedes a read-only check, so the expected immediate write conflicts with the skill's protocol.
findings.fix: Make this a two-turn eval: first require a proposed safe ordering and no file write; then supply approval and verify the generated command follows that approved order, including a cleanliness check before checkout/pull. Update the expected output and ordering assertion accordingly.

findings.evidence: The side-effect skeleton defines only "Already done: continue to step 6" and "Not done: show the error and ask before one retry." Following the branch where the state query itself fails or times out reaches no defined outcome; neither does a timeout of the permitted retry. SKILL.md prohibits blind retries, but this reusable skeleton leaves the corresponding recovery and reporting behavior unspecified.
findings.fix: Add explicit outcomes for confirmed completion, confirmed absence, unknown state, and conflicting or partial completion. Stop and report uncertainty or conflict without retrying; after an approved retry fails or times out, repeat the state check and report success only when completion is verified.
